newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT says postal sales up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT says postal sales up 10 pct.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland said on Tuesday its postal activities boosted turnover by 10 percent in 1996, due mainly to acquisitions.
Operating profits rose 30.8 percent to 943 million guilders, partly reflecting one-off factors, it said.
"Turnover of 6.71 billion was booked, 10.4 percent more than in the previous year...Of the turnover growth, more than half was due to acquisitions," KPN said in a statement.
The group earlier reported 1996 net profit rose to 2.46 billion guilders from a year-earlier 2.26 billion.

It said the most important buys were its Belgian Distribution service, Net courier services in Germany, Austria and Denmark and the takeover of Dutch bookshop and stationery chains De Boekelier and Bruna by its 50 percent-owned Postkantoren BV.
Its successful bid for the shares of Australia's TNT had made PTT Post one of the world's big four in time-sensitive distribution and logistical services, it added.
It said it added 528 million guilders to restructuring reserves in 1996 in an ongoing drive to cut costs.
